title: Fncall parsing debug - scratchpad and breadcrumbs
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal breadcrumbs while investigating repeated parsing failures when validating tool-call responses from hosted API (mostly observed in playground + a couple of customer repros).
- This is messy, iterative notes to self. Not a runbook yet.

Timeline / high-level summary:
- 2026-03-02: Customer report (via support thread) - tooling agent returns malformed JSON in 'tool_output' field intermittently. Ticket JIRA: INFR-1123.
- 2026-03-03..03-05: Repro attempts in local dev & staging; sometimes works locally, fails on staging runtime 2/5.
- 2026-03-07: Initial suspicion: tokenization/stream-chunk boundary causing truncated JSON.
- 2026-03-09: Found second class of failures: model emits valid JSON but with trailing comments ("//") and unquoted keys -> our strict parser rejects.

Repro steps I've used locally (notes + commands tried):
1) Basic curl to hosted endpoint (simulating function call):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/generate \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model":"open-fn-v1","input":"call tool get_price(product_id=123)"}' \
   -> got response with tool_call block; tool_output appears truncated end: '...\"price\": 9.99,' and then socket closed.

2) Python streaming client (requests + iter_content) to observe chunk framing:
   # snippet (local):
   r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, stream=True)
   for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
       print('CHUNK>', repr(chunk))

   -> observed last chunk sometimes b'\\n\\n{"tool_output": "{\"price\": 9.99,', then connection close.
   Hypothesis: serving runtime sometimes flushes/encodes chunks in a way that our consumer concatenation drops final bytes.

3) Try tolerant parsing on client (python):
   # allow trailing commas and comments by pre-cleanup
   text = re.sub(r'//.*', '', raw)
   text = re.sub(r',\s*}', '}', text)
   parsed = json.loads(text)
   -> fixed some cases; but not safe as a general fix.

4) Reproduction on staging with specific seed (staging uses model variant open-fn-v1-q4b). Run script that repeats 200 requests (sleep=10ms)
   -> failure rate ~3%. Failure modes:
   - mode A: truncated bytes (JSON cut mid-value)
   - mode B: valid JSON but non-standard syntax (trailing comma / unquoted keys)

Error snippets seen (copied raw):
- "...\"tool_output\": \"{\"price\": 9.99,\""
"
- "{\"tool_output\": "{price: 9.99, \"currency\": \"USD\"}"}"
- stack (client): ValueError: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 3 (char 2)

Hypotheses so far (ranked):
1) Serving runtime chunking edge-case: the stream encoder sometimes breaks inside multi-byte sequences when using gzip/deflate or when adapting packet sizes -> client gets broken UTF-8 and JSON parse fails. (prob: 0.6)
2) Model output sanitization mismatch: some model variants are configured to emit debug-friendly JS-style objects (looser formatting) for certain tool-call prompts. (prob: 0.2)
3) Middleware post-processing bug: a transformer in the pipeline that post-processes tool outputs (e.g., pretty-printer) inserts comments or trailing commas when output length > threshold. (prob: 0.15)
4) Customer agent injecting content via tool args causing model to echo unescaped tokens. (prob: 0.05)

Investigation notes / things I've checked:
- Confirmed client concat logic is simple: bytes_buffer += chunk; decode after stream end. (Rina confirmed via quick code check). So probably not a concat bug on our side but still possible if chunk boundaries drop bytes due to streaming semantics.
- Checked NGINX proxy logs on staging: no 4xx/5xx around failures; upstream connection closed normally.
- Captured tcpdump on staging for a failing session -> reassembled TCP stream shows JSON truncated mid-utf8 sequence (observed invalid utf-8 sequence at EOF).
- Looked at runtime streaming code (runtime/streaming/encoder.py) -> uses .write(buffer) to socket, then flush; there is a code path that optionally compresses chunks when size > 16KB. Found a TODO about "ensure chunk alignment for multibyte encodings".
- Re-ran with compression disabled (env var STREAM_COMPRESSION=0 on staging) for 10k requests -> failure rate drops to 0.1%. That suggests compression interaction.

Additional oddity (non-truncation failures):
- Some responses are semantically invalid JS-style (unquoted keys): reproduced when using model variant open-fn-v1-debug. These variants are on staging only and have a special prompt tweak (dev-only). Suspect the model was fine but pre/post prompt templates allowed it to produce a JS-ish object.

Quick experiments to mitigate on client-side (temporary):
- Implement tolerant parser wrapper: attempt json.loads(raw); on JSONDecodeError, try fixups: strip trailing commas, remove // comments, add quotes to simple keys via regex. Works for ~85% of broken payloads in testing but masks root cause.
- For truncated bytes: try incremental decoding using 'surrogatepass' error handler to retain bytes and attempt to recover with heuristics. Too fragile for production.

Proposed short-term remediation (what I will push):
- Force disable streaming compression for hosted API customers until streaming encoder fix is deployed. (Low impact, medium perf cost).
- Add defensive reassembly on client libs: keep last 512 bytes of prior chunk and attempt to re-decode on failure with surrogate handling (non-ideal but buys time).
- Add detection/metrics for "incomplete-json-after-stream-close" and tag by model variant / runtime shard.

Long-term fixes / TODOs (tracked on INFR-1123):
- runtime: fix chunk encoding logic to ensure multibyte characters are not split across compressed chunk boundaries (runtime/streaming/encoder.py). Add unit test that compresses known multibyte payload and asserts decoder correctness.
- model config: ensure dev-only variants do not have prompt templates that allow JS-style outputs for tool calls. Audit model onboarding docs.
- client libs: publish 'fncall-tolerant-parser' util in python/js SDKs with warnings and opt-in.

Open questions / ask SRE/product folks:
- Is it acceptable to disable compression for hosted streaming temporarily? (Latency/egress cost tradeoff). Need signoff from infra team.
- Are there any customers actively using debug model variants on staging that may have contributed to noise? Rina to confirm.

Notes to self (quick actions):
- [ ] Add metric in observability for json-parse-failures-from-stream (tag: model, runtime-shard) - ticket created INF-OBS-522.
- [x] Reproduce with STREAM_COMPRESSION=0 locally -> reduces failures (done 2026-03-10).
- [ ] Draft small PR to runtime to add chunk-alignment test + simple fix (branch: fix/encoder-chunk-boundary).
- [ ] Add client tolerant parser as opt-in in SDK 1.9.0.

Snippets to paste into PRs / tickets: (keep as raw examples)
- truncated example:
  "...\"tool_output\": \"{\"price\": 9.99,\""

- unquoted-keys example:
  {tool_output: "{price: 9.99, currency: \"USD\"}"}

If I come back later: quick checklist to triage a new report:
1) collect raw http body (not just parsed) + request id + model variant + runtime shard
2) try reproduce with/without STREAM_COMPRESSION
3) tcpdump/reassemble to see if truncation at TCP level or above
4) check runtime encoder logs for compression branch for that request id
5) try tolerant parser to surface full payload if safe

End of scratchpad.

-- aisha
